summary: Recorded receipt a20ffdbaf258403c8f0c6a4d4c141e1f, the repeat execution of the fixed heartbeat jitter experiment from its retained inputs. The fourth pair of arms reproduced both readings: the no-delay case inverted once in 200 attempts (final term 400, max delay 0) and the jittered case inverted 98 times (final term 303, max delay 2 ms). The no-delay counts are now 0, 0, 2 and 1 across four independent runs, so the inversion recurs without any added delay and no longer rests on a single anomalous run; the jittered counts of 90, 97, 105 and 98 stay in a fifteen-event band out of four hundred. The account keeps its violated conclusion and asserted defect claim, the counterevidence entry now states three of eight hundred no-delay attempts against ninety to one hundred and five of two hundred with jitter, and the limitation is rewritten to describe the zero-delay estimate as small but recurrent, bounding the order of magnitude rather than the rate. The joint history records that this receipt is a repeat of the same fixed experiment, sharing case names, admissions and assertions with the earlier three runs and differing only in scheduler behaviour. Both heartbeat knowledge entries gain the receipt, knowledge-0 on the case events and knowledge-1 on the result events, at the resulting revisions six and eight.
